inventions: What Things Cost opening: the Broth Suit of Year 702. Hob Ladleworth, a Stannvaard saddlers'-market cookshop keeper, against Scarlet Oriel Thrane, a Journeyman fighter, over a bowl of broth. The magistrate's list, cried by a herald over three days, is made the origin of the price list.

Value, Coin and Trade opening: the wreck of the carrack Fat Marguerite on the Gannet Bar in Year 697. Tamsin Reedmace is her bonded Journeyman weather-worker. Each item that came ashore illustrates one line of the Arbitration Division's order of payment.

News, Rumor opening: Long Cuddy Ouzel of the Bluecap Yard (a fighting school), who 'died three times' in Year 706 after killing the bounty target called the Tin Deacon at Marrowford. Includes the nine-word beacon message and the funeral on Cooper's Hill.
News, Rumor: the Ridge towers' strike of Year 698, over the winter ration.

Item names in the price table: 'war crossbow' (lever-spanned, or heavy windlass arbalest), 'belt-bow' (short crossbow spanned from the belt, successor to the revolver), 'sheaf of bolts', 'news bill', 'a seat on a kept road' (open bench or under the hood, successors to third and first class).

News, Rumor terms: beacon-house (old gauge-house), beacon boy (old wire-boy), the heralds' rate and the heralds' night watch (old press rate and night press wires), post riders' yellow sashes, hiring a relay rider for one bag.

News, Rumor new material under R83-7: sections on heralds and criers, minstrels, bounties, bookies and what fame does; a second reference table on how each voice moves and goes wrong; three new hooks (the bill still on the door, the price that moved, the song that will not die).

Value, Coin and Trade: a new 'Fame moves the schedule' paragraph under Rank as Property (R83-7). Array-tenders on a keeper's Core are named as what 'delivery' of an Essence supply contract means. The Essence price is now cried from guild hall steps on quarter-day.
Author Notes in News, Rumor: real-world precedents added (Leo the Mathematician's beacon chain with matched clocks, Chappe's semaphore, the Mongol yam, the Persian royal road).

calls.call: A sheaf of bolts is priced at 1 to 2 silver the dozen. The old cartridge row read 1 to 2 silver the fifty. The silver figure stays and the count changes.
calls.grounds: The brief's settled figure is about three coppers a bolt, and it is also in Who Pays for the Lamp and the staged Bolt page. At fifty for 1 to 2 silver a bolt would cost under a copper. A dozen at 1 to 2 silver gives 2 to 4 copper each. The brief's 'keep prices' rule and its three-copper figure collide here, so the specific settled figure governs.

calls.call: The beacon message price and the old nine-word form are both kept: a silver buys twenty words with addresses counted, addresses take eleven on an ordinary day, and that leaves the nine-word standard form.
calls.grounds: What Things Cost and Who Pays for the Lamp say a silver for twenty words with addresses counted. The old News page and the Accord and Stannvaard inventories say nine words. Reading nine as what remains after addresses keeps every figure without changing either source.

calls.call: The price of Essence, the supply contract and the standing myriad stay, with all figures (40 silver marks, 12 at Year 640). Delivery is restated as a keeper's Core plus a bonded crew of array-tenders who pull, refine and feed the works.
calls.grounds: Arrays survive section one as standing runed workings (NATALIE, The Magic System pages), and the contract is the page's central economic fact. The brief retires mains and tariffs on supply, not contracts for work by living hands. Keeping the ledger and changing only what delivery means loses nothing.

calls.call: The array boom and copper famine stay, and copper remains 'the wire of the array trade' in the sense of metal wire laid by hand. Only the signal wire is retired.
calls.grounds: Copper famines are cited in What Things Cost and elsewhere. Metal wire and windings are medieval craft, and the brief retires the telegraph.

calls.call: The duplicated 'industrialisation of Essence' passage in Rank as Property is merged into one. It now reads 'The un-Tempered laborer of the Dark Ages is worse off than his Voyager-era ancestor'. The garbled second copy ('late Imperial Age ... Imperial-era ancestor') is dropped.
calls.grounds: The second copy was a leftover from an earlier mechanical rename and carried no separate fact. The first copy's Voyager comparison makes sense; the second's does not.

calls.call: Land is now priced on 'the Wellspring site beneath it', and Nalūn sits on 'sites of Contract-aspected Wellsprings'. A parenthesis gives R83-9's definition.
calls.grounds: R83-9: Wellsprings are types of Aether with sites where they pool. The argument that land is priced on what lies beneath is unchanged.

calls.call: Banking at Ironlink becomes 'keeping its strongboxes at Ironlink'. Lending houses become money-changers and factor houses. In the retainer table, 'merchant house' becomes 'factor house', 'a bank' becomes 'a money-changers' house', 'a Board' or 'charter Board' becomes 'a chartered company', and 'shipping line' becomes 'a shipowner'.
calls.grounds: The group note and R83-4 place banks and merchant houses in the Imperial Age. Factor houses already appear in section one's pages.

calls.call: The Bill table uses Who Pays for the Lamp's terms: sealed household and trade work at the same figures, with snuffers and the searcher replacing the cutter and the inspector. The 'cut plate, four seconds to lift' line becomes 'a stroke through a ward costs nothing to make and takes four seconds'.
calls.grounds: The group note requires agreement with Who Pays for the Lamp, which has snuffers scratching through wards. The four seconds and the zero cost survive.

calls.call: The heading 'Arms and Shot' became 'Arms and Bolts'. Headings in News, Rumor changed ('I. The Wire' to 'I. The Beacon Line', 'The press rate' to 'The heralds' rate').
calls.grounds: The brief retires shot and wire. A grep found no anchor links to these headings anywhere in wiki/, imports/drafts/wiki-rewrite/ or NATALIE.

calls.call: The Guild-hour mechanism follows the Sky, the Hour and the Year wording: great water clock at Stannvaard, relay rider, sealed sand-glass, beacons. Northern clerks keep Guild hour 'for the relays'.
calls.grounds: That page already carries the converted wording, and the two must agree.

calls.call: 'Across the water: same day where cable exists' becomes 'same day where island towers carry the line'. The timings stay.
calls.grounds: Cable is retired with the wire. A beacon chain over water needs islands, and the figure is kept where one exists.

calls.call: The Struck 2026-09-12 note about Nevara stays verbatim, and the era headings (Antediluvian through the Withering) stay.
calls.grounds: It records a past canon strike, and those eras survive in the Concordance of Ages. The brief does not retire them.

canon_conflicts: Bolt price: the old table's cartridges at 1 to 2 silver the fifty against the brief's three coppers a bolt. Handled by changing the count to the dozen; see calls.
Beacon word count: twenty words in What Things Cost and Who Pays for the Lamp against nine words in News and the inventories. Reconciled in text; see calls.
desktop/inventories/accord.md still treats the wire, the main, the meter and the Board as live, against R83. It may rank below the wiki in practice, and this rewrite follows the brief.
other_pages_needing_change: desktop/inventories/accord.md, desktop/inventories/stannvaard.md, desktop/inventories/dawi.md: still use the wire, the main, the nine-word wire, the meter and wire-boys. These need beacon line, sealed-household and beacon-boy wording. All are outside the staged wiki.

Staged 'The Apparatus of the Age' page (another agent's group): when grepped mid-run it still carried the bolt-action repeater and the press section, including 'Guild gazettes three copper, penny papers one'. It should match the news-bill row here: a news bill at 1 copper, the Guild's copied sheets at 3.

Staged 'The Bolt and the Enhanced Weapon' page (another agent's group, apparently renamed from Shot and the Enhanced Weapon): should use the same purchase units as the price table, the quiver of twenty and the sheaf of a dozen. The launching session should check that the rename does not break the brief's validator path.

wiki/Materials, Alchemy & Trade/Work, Trade and Measure/The Works and Days and Weight, Measure and the Standard: both contain Guild hour or nine-word references and should say relays or the beacon line (another group).
desktop/style-bank/lineage-halls.md line 243 (a measure-wire) is ordinary metal wire and needs no change. Noted only so it is not flagged.

inventions: Alchemy.md: the Riser that let go at Gannet Row in the second year of the Dark Ages, and the sky-blue salt sold back at forty coppers the sack.

Alchemetrica: Corbin Oakapple, apothecary of Candle Wharf; the House of Merrowby and its Rising Salt (Sublimatio married to Fixatio); the Rivermen's Regatta; the nine-day hanging wreck and the chandler's widow with her ladder; the Hanging Fair; Merrowby's pears and card.
Alchemetrica, street slang (R82-39): a bad marriage (Rupture Event), a bottle (a Draft), a dry hand (an alchemist with no woken Crystal).
Alchemetrica: bead-glasses and clay trial-cones as the medieval heat instruments; a house's beer and song at the Mark; the long shelf of Returners.
The Standing Index: Lord Bartholomew the granary cat; Maudlin Purslane; Jos Tolliver; Ser Bevis Hatchard; the Marrowgate assize; the case Purslane against Tolliver; the Ratcatchers' Company.
The Common Drafts: the wreck of the Dorcas Merry on the Skerrow Teeth; the village of Skerrow; Goody Nettlebed; Wat Cobbold.
The Common Drafts, street slang: a swallow (fight Draft), a scald (an above-grade Draft).
Prepared Tags: Tamsin Cordwain of Quenby, Fulk Pyke, the Company of the Slate, the Cutters' Stair, the funeral with its thirty-one forged tags, and the children's skipping rhyme.
Prepared Tags, street slang: a slap, a strip (a tag).
All invented figures are minor and of past or unspecified generations. Full names were grepped against wiki/ with no hit. No main cast, sealed secrets or arc events are used.

calls.call: Alchemetrica's 'No Draft refills a reserve' now reads 'Only a fight Draft refills a reserve'. The sickroom half of the old law stays: the Bench refuses restorative sickroom formulas, and nothing brewed for the sickroom puts Essence back.
calls.grounds: RULINGS.md answer 101 (EC2, 2026-09-28) and R2-6 said no Draft refills. Isaac's later direction R78-10 retracted that for fight Drafts, and R79-10 says 'A fight Draft refills reserve and the crash pays for it'. NATALIE's Magic Frame says the same, and section one's Tier Ladders already reads 'Only a fight Draft refills a reserve.' Newest word wins. Worded to match the Tier Ladders. The session that launched me should log it.

calls.call: Alchemetrica no longer uses 'current' for a Wellspring anywhere. The Wellspring is defined per R83-9 as a type of Aether affecting the Crystal, a source of power that also represents an alchemical principle and a spiritual transformation. Stages 'take their law from' a Wellspring, and the table column 'Current' is now 'Wellspring'. 'Living process, law of transformation' stays, as the Family register keeps it.
calls.grounds: Group note and R83-9. The Eight Families page gives the same reading ('a type of Aether that carries a fixed law', 'each of the sixty is a living process, a law of transformation'). A link to that page was added.

calls.call: Vein Draw, Vital Draw and Sovereign Draw stay as Provenance Class names alongside Crystal Draw. A short note under the heading explains 'Draw' as the bench's old word for a lot taken off its source, with no connection to how a practitioner pulls Aether. The lowercase 'Class V draw' and 'drawing off a donor' were reworded.
calls.grounds: The group note keeps Crystal Draw as a materials grade. The four names are one series, and renaming three would break the Class table and the materials pages.

calls.call: 'Vein' and 'array' stay. A vein is the channel feeding a place where one type of Aether pools, and an array is a standing runed working. Only 'arrays pump' went, and 'arrays draw from the veins' became 'pull off the veins'. 'Engine work' stays too.
calls.grounds: Section one's Tier Ladders keeps 'a vein is the channel that feeds it'. Arrays survive in NATALIE's boost law and The Four Crafts. The Mechanica page keeps engine work, and only 'draw-engines' is retired.

calls.call: Retired instruments and arms were replaced in place. The gauge became the assay fork. Glass thermometers, thermocouples and pyrometers became bead-glasses and clay trial-cones; the point that every instrument reads the bed and never the charge survives. Enhanced shot and the enhanced round became enhanced bolts at the same price. Ordnance became proofed harness and siege stores. 'Printed on nothing' became 'written on nothing'. 'Industrialised' became 'bagged by the gross in a Guild workshop'.
calls.grounds: Brief's retired table and the 'instruments are medieval' line. Keep-prices rule.

calls.call: 'Dead ground' stays as a tag-trade term, redefined as salted ground, bled ground, a place beside a closed Core, or a place no Wellspring's Aether reaches. 'The main' became kept streets and kept cities.
calls.grounds: Brief's replacement for 'cut the main', and section one's Runes and Tags fuel table.

calls.call: The coil stays, glossed as the brass assay instrument. Coilwright's Reading Oil, Metering Tonic and the Tiers and prices are unchanged. 'A militia charge' became 'a charge a militia throws'.
calls.grounds: Section one keeps the coil, and the group note keeps item names and prices. Other pages treat Onceglass charges as thrown or loosed militia stock, so the entry survives without implying a cell.

calls.call: The item names Grey Standing Chalk and Bone-Grey Compress keep their spelling. The cover-name 'The Grey Bride' became 'The Gray Bride'.
calls.grounds: The group note keeps item names, and both items appear on other groups' pages (Materials, Alchemy & Trade.md, The Long March). The cover-name appears on no item row, so American spelling applies. Isaac can order a global rename if he wants one.

calls.call: Several 'not X, Y' fragments in table rows were rephrased with their facts kept (Found and never rendered; Reveals forgery; It enforces and it wants nothing; the forfeiture clause and sentencing line; the two-phial rule). Em dashes in prose were removed. The one remaining em dash in The Standing Index is the empty table cell on The Unnamed Ninth.
calls.grounds: Brief, 'The page itself'.

canon_conflicts: Prepared Tags vs section one's Runes and Tags: Prepared Tags says ambient and stored tags light in the maker's color and are cut on paper, leather or slate. Runes and Tags says a tag flares in the user's color and is cut on paper, hide, bark or thin foil. Left as it stands on my page, and the Prepared Tags opening story depends on the maker's-color rule. Not logged.

The Standing Index header says forty-five entries, but the tables hold forty-six rows. The Tier Ladder and the Unnamed Ninth row say four T9 entries, but five T9 rows exist (Worldspirit Quench, Concordant's Oblation, Apex Residue, Null-Absolute Solvent, The Unnamed Ninth). Pre-existing; left unchanged and not logged.

Cutwater Tincture is Class III in The Standing Index and 'Environmental' in The Common Drafts. Hillcarry Salts is Class II Field Substrate in the Index and 'Material-Sourced' in the Drafts. Pre-existing; left unchanged and not logged.

RULINGS.md answer 101 (EC2) and CONFLICTS C-096 record 'no Draft refills a reserve' as ruled, while R78-10 and R79-10 reverse it for fight Drafts. See calls; the C-096 entry should be read as superseded.
other_pages_needing_change: wiki/The War Cycle/The Army/The Long March.md: per CONFLICTS C-096 it repeats 'A practitioner is refilled by a Wellspring, or not at all', which needs the fight Draft exception.
Materials, Alchemy & Trade/Alchemy/The Heresiology of Alchemy.md (another group): one line still contains 'current'. It should match Alchemetrica's 'cut from the Wellspring whose law it works'.

Work, Trade and Measure pages (The Works and Days; The Apparatus of the Age) and Hide, Horn and Bone: their Onceglass charges, 'consumable munitions', 'volley' and 'battery' language should agree with 'a charge a militia throws'.
The Magic System/Power in Use/Runes and Tags.md: the tag color and material lines should be squared with Prepared Tags.

inventions: Works and Days opening: the funeral of Ranulf Scarrow, the Anvil-Eater, grandmaster of the Scarlet Rams of Harrowgate; the rival Blue Herons of Lower Harrowgate and their song 'Who'll Wash the Ram?'; Elder Maud Bretton; Gammer Thirza Lubbock and the thirty-one layer-outs; a herring-bone death; Harrowgate's Long Market and Tanners' Row. All names grepped clear of wiki/.

New section 'The Small Powers': Cold-Wife, Link-Child, Knot-Wife, Bone-Thumb, Sour-Stopper, Mule-Talker, Whetter, Hush-Nurse, with invented copper prices (1 to 4 copper; 1 silver a ship's lashing; 2 silver a sword) set against the 3-copper loaf and the 12 to 24 copper day wage; the Measurewright's folios on the Cold-Wife's palm; Dame Mabel Madder's Self-Minding Cradle.
New section 'The Yard and the Token': sect ranks as a working morning, built on Training and Sects, with the retainer figures copied from What Things Cost.
New section 'What the Trades Are Paid': wages copied from What Things Cost and Who Pays for the Lamp, plus the pay statements already on the page. No new figures.
New trades in the Evening Trades table: the Herald and the Crier, the Minstrel, the Bookie, the Bounty-Clerk (R83-7).

Weight, Measure opening: the grain cog Fat Margery bursting at the Barley Fair of Saltby, the thirty-one-year suit, Rolling Ned Tolland the strike-board man, Margery's Acre. Arithmetic follows the page: 500 loads level is 625 heaped, 5,000 measures at eight to the load.
Weight, Measure: the true-hand, a petty art that hefts a weight to the grain at a copper the call.
Hub opening: the Vintners and the Coopers of Rushford and their feud over the tun, on the Long Quay.

Weight §VII: the ferrule redefined as a bronze ring set at a Core's lip, the draught as that bore on ground of a stated grade for one Guild hour by the water clock, and the tundish as a brass fitting on the ring that shows the color of what passes.
The sleeping sponge (poppy, mandrake, henbane) and vinegar with spirits of wine as the medieval successors of anesthesia and carbolic.

calls.call: Reconciled 'one in twelve' on this page with 'about one in ten wake a Crystal' in How Magic Works, The Gate and Who Pays for the Lamp. One in twelve is ranked with a token; the difference is woken people with one petty art and no token.
calls.grounds: Both figures are on the wiki. R83-8 and R83-10 need common practitioners and an unranked petty class. Both figures are kept, and the gap is explained rather than either being changed.

calls.call: The creditor schedule line 'behind only contracted Essence supply' now reads 'contracted Essence (bonded work and Core hours already sold)'.
calls.grounds: Supply is retired by the brief. The ordering of the schedule is kept. No other page carries this line.

calls.call: Kept the unit name 'draught' with its British spelling as a keepers' term of art, with an in-world aside that the spelling keeps it apart from a Draft. Heading VII became 'The Draught'. Ferrule and tundish survive with new physical meanings.
calls.grounds: Nothing lost, and the unit does not depend on the retired idea of the draw. The Working Vocabulary (section one) already keeps the tundish, and the Articles of the Accord still name the ferrule. 'Draft' would collide with the bottled working. Ordinary uses went American ('draftsman', 'draft beast'), and the Farmer's 'halves the draught' became 'halves the labor of the team'.

calls.call: Weights-and-measures inspectors became searchers in the Weight page (searcher's stamp, market searcher).
calls.grounds: The brief maps old inspectors to searchers, and 'searcher' was a real medieval market office. This extends the word from fee inspection to market inspection.

calls.call: Banks were avoided: the Engravers' lock joke now reads 'counting-houses', the Holy Sea's 'banking operations' read 'deposit-and-lending operations', and the retainer table's 'a bank' reads 'a counting-house'.
calls.grounds: R83-4 gives banks to the Imperial Age. The Holy Sea and Nalūn dispute is kept. 'Merchant house' stays in the retainer table because What Things Cost has it and factor houses are medieval, though R83-4 also gives merchant houses to the Imperial Age, so the launching session may want a line on it.

calls.call: The Theater and Music Hall became the Playhouse and the (tavern) Hall, with the same chairman, comic singer, strong man and closing turn. The Café became the Tea-Stall. Fireworks became a hired hand throwing colored fire, since gunpowder is retired. The balloon ascent became a rope-walker on a Vectoria line. The cinematograph booth became a shadow-play booth, keeping the 'only moving pictures' joke.
calls.grounds: Brief: no gunpowder, nothing built beyond medieval. What Things Cost already sells tea at a stall.

calls.call: The Reconstruction, arrays, the Withering, the brass coil, Core-keeper fees and the Guild hour stay as they were.
calls.grounds: None is on the retired list. Section one keeps the coil and arrays, and The Sky, the Hour and the Year keeps the Guild hour on water clocks. Mine arrays are kept as hand-tended glyph works, and tenders keep their gaskets, conduit junctions and wrench, because Brida Voss's epigraph is a kept joke.

calls.call: Removed the verbatim duplicate of the closing two blockquote paragraphs of Works and Days. Heavy negation cousins ('None of that is metaphor... It is a law', 'Not a hotel. A social institution', 'Not extraction. Trust.', 'is not superstition. It is observation') were rewritten with the same facts.
calls.grounds: Brief's page rules. The duplicate was a copy error with no facts of its own.

calls.call: Replaced 'WOTR should copy it exactly' and 'carries more worldbuilding' in the Weight page with in-world wording. Kept 'exactly as the real world ran troy against avoirdupois' and the Hooks section.
calls.grounds: Narrator stays in-world where touched, while Who Pays for the Lamp still keeps a craft section (Writing It), so reader-facing hooks are allowed.

canon_conflicts: Articles of the Accord, Title IV 'Of the Draw' (Articles XVI to XVIII: 'on any service', 'every housing fitted', 'seal on a conduit', 'Cut off') still uses the retired metered-supply language. Weight §VII now reads ferrule, tundish and draught as Core-side terms. Those articles need the matching conversion, and I did not touch them.

What Things Cost (live copy and the staged copy when read) still says draw, wire, rail, muskets, Boards and 'Guild inspector'. My pay table and retainer table copy its figures, using searcher, company and counting-house for the payers. Its sibling rewrite should end up with the same figures and payer words.
R83-4 says the Imperial Age brings banks and merchant houses, while the wiki's Dark Ages pages have factor houses, Nalūn bills and Holy Sea lending. Treated as medieval precursors, not resolved.

inventions: Heresiology opening: Odger Marrable, master dyer of Hartle Ferry, and his Marrable Red (a recipe lost for good); the spagyrist Tamsin Corbie; the double funeral of 661 IC, with sixty gold paid by his three daughters. Dyers' Row and the story of the abbot's horse belong to the same story. A grep of wiki/ found no use of Odger, Marrable, Tamsin, Corbie or Hartle.
Heresiology: the dock slang 'gone to the mirror' for a corrupted alchemist.
Heresiology: the archivist-narrator who has carried the book for twenty-two years.

Heresiology: the Grade I and Grade IV aside. Petty cases: a hedge-worker's overcharged well charm, a stall-holder's tincture that was mostly plum, a lamp-warden's boy cutting a stolen glyph. Grade IV is cried by heralds, with bounties on hand-copied bills and minstrels who get it wrong.
Heresiology: the Measurewrights' and confessors' dispute over the word 'injury', with the Accord choosing the word so that both parties could sign.

Real Alchemy: the bench children's skipping rhyme for the seven stages ('Burn it, drown it, part it, wed it, / rot it, raise it, set it, dread it'), including the eighth verb as the apprentices' addition.
Real Alchemy: a Judicium reader as the nearest thing a WOTR court has to a poison test. This is inferred from the Fulguria page's mechanism for Judicium.

calls.call: The Real Alchemy stays an out-of-world reference page with no Guild narrator, and it opens on real history: HMS Triumph at Cadiz in 1810, then Newton, Boerhaave, Vallot and Louis XIV, Stewart and Principe.
calls.grounds: The page is real-world history with sources, and the hub page Alchemy.md quotes its 'out-of-world' subtitle. An invented opening would blur the line between sourced fact and fiction. Every opening fact except the Cadiz location comes from the page's own entries, and Cadiz comes from its Earles 1964 citation. The brief's narrator rule says the narrator 'stays', and this page never had one, so it gets a warm, opinionated authorial voice instead.

calls.call: Pyrometers, thermocouples, Seger's cones, thermometers, borosilicate glass and the Marsh and Reinsch tests stay in the real-history practice text. Their In WOTR lines now say none of them exists in any era of WOTR. The old claims that they exist from 690 IC, or fall inside the Imperial Age's technology span, and the citations to R53-01 and R63-2, are gone.
calls.grounds: R83 and NATALIE: what is built and carried stays medieval. The brief lists instruments as assay forks, water clocks, brass and glass. Removing borosilicate also removes the conflict the old page said it would not settle against Alchemetrica's account of glass, so that sentence went too. The 820 °C softening figure moved into the practice text and survives.

calls.call: The real-history accident row 'trial batch of chlorate gunpowder' (Essonnes, 1788) stays word for word. The In WOTR line beneath it now says WOTR has no guns and no gunpowder in any era. These are the only uses of 'gunpowder' or 'guns' in the two files.
calls.grounds: Brief: nothing is lost unless retired, and the retirement concerns the WOTR setting. This is a real historical record on an out-of-world page. Printing, 'the imperial pint' and similar real-world facts stay on the same grounds.

calls.call: 'From 690 IC' appears once on The Real Alchemy, as the opening of the Dark Ages. The In WOTR lines are framed as the Dark Ages bench.
calls.grounds: The group's notes and the brief's dates.

calls.call: The Stage-to-Wellspring mapping uses only what the Family index gives: Calcination/Cinerion, Dissolution/Dissolution, Separation/Judicium, Conjunction/none (runs on Attraction), Fermentation/Rebirthine, Distillation/Sublimare, Coagulation/Coagulatio. Trade's-reading lines are quoted from the Alchemy lines on the Family pages and marked as the trade's reading.

calls.grounds: Brief's prose bans, plus nothing lost and keep the good jokes. The Family pages quote the Heresiology's shadow and purification doctrine, and those lines still agree. The Tenebra line now reads 'no proof of heresy', which is the Family page's wording.

calls.call: Reference bolt keeps the revolver's figures: 16 g, about 235 m/s, about 440 J, 43 ms over ten meters, assigned to the steel-bowed windlass arbalest. The enhancer table is unchanged. An ordinary hand-spanned bolt is about 100 J and flies slower, with no speed figure given.
calls.grounds: The group note and brief say each item keeps its figure, and 440 J for the heavy arbalest and 100 J for the ordinary bolt were settled in section one. A real steel bow throws far heavier bolts far slower, so the page carries the quarrel openly as a bowyer against Measurewright argument (R83-11). Isaac may want the velocities re-derived.

calls.call: The D row of the speed table changed. Old: registers it and may begin to turn, it hits. New: the brief's exact Grade D wording plus 'A bolt they do not see hits them.' The E, C and B results stand, and the brief's exact Grade B wording is added to the B row.
calls.grounds: The brief's exact wording for Grade D says a D-Grade can slip the bolt if they see the loose, which contradicts the old cell. D's 15 to 40 ms reaction against a 43 ms flight supports the new wording.

calls.call: The old Apparatus line 'A C-Grade practitioner can react to gunfire and cannot outrun it' became the Grade D and Grade B wordings, and the C-Grade sentence is gone.

calls.call: Musket ball becomes a rampart arbalest's dart, a wall-mounted bow at 400 m/s and up, keeping the law that C reacts without outrunning and B dodges reliably, and that catching takes upper B or reliable A.
